comparison: Strong disagreement on speculative claims (C7, C82, C93, C95) about concurrent transcription and immune evasion. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct experimental validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, explicitly requesting empirical demonstration of assumptions and noting no mechanistic knowledge emerges.

Disagreement on validation experiment (C83-C91). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the time-course comparison and NP explanation convincing. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting 'very little was done' experimentally and 'one would have expected more' validation work.

Disagreement on experimental design rationale (C53, C105-C109). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the justification for early timepoint and cRNA timing reasonable based on citations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting empirical demonstration that cRNA production does not occur within 2 hours.

Significant disagreement on methodological framework (C3, C4, C36, C38, C40, C54-C56). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding experimental data validates the conceptual framework. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting the model 'built on several assumptions...lacking experimental support' and provides only 'partial support.'

Disagreement on kinetic model and export rates (C5, C6, C39, C59-C61, C76-C81). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding model fitting and parameter estimation well-supported. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether model adds understanding beyond FISH observations and noting 'export rate is an ambiguous number.'

Agreement on imaging data quality (C45-C47, C50, C57, C62-C64). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for quantitative measurements and heterogeneity observations. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging FISH data and identifying the technique as a strength, with no challenges to raw imaging data.

Partial agreement on broader applications (C96-C104). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for logical extensions of methodology. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the approach 'could be useful' but noting broader applicability is a projection rather than demonstrated result.

Both address mechanistic gaps (C111-C117, C121, C123, C125). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for identifying discrepancies with NXF1 dependencies. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting 'one is left with more questions since no mechanistic knowledge emerges' and lack of experimental follow-up.

Agreement on speculative nature of mechanistic proposals (C110, C122-C128). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting mechanistic proposals are speculative. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of mechanistic knowledge and additional experimentation needed.

Disagreement on cRNA contamination claims (C52-C53). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding temporal argument and citations sufficient. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting empirical demonstration of the cRNA timing assumption.

OpenEval finds stochastic variation concept and time-course validation (C65-C68, C70, C73-C74) SUPPORTED by Figure 3 data showing cells progress along predicted trajectory. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval finds experimental setup and 2D approximation validation (C42-C44, C48-C49) SUPPORTED by Z-distribution analysis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these technical validation claims.

OpenEval finds claims about splicing and intron detection (C118-C121) SUPPORTED, appropriately identifying limitations while drawing reasonable conclusions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific technical points.

OpenEval finds framing claims about study contributions (C1, C2, C8, C41) SUPPORTED as appropriate representation of scope. No specific peer review evaluation of these high-level framing claims, though C8 and C41 appear tangentially in peer reviews of other claim groups.
